claims.text: A machine-learning model incorporating phonon dispersion relations can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed model uses phonon dispersion relations to predict phonon thermal conductivity.
Phonon dispersion relations describe the relationship between phonon frequency and wavevector.
High-entropy alloys have distinctive properties that affect phonon scattering.
Incorporating high-entropy-alloy effects on phonon scattering will improve prediction accuracy.
The model will improve prediction accuracy by an estimated 15–25% relative to current predictions.
Current predictions of phonon thermal conductivity for the targeted high-entropy alloys are inaccurate.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys used under thermal-insulation conditions.
The approach may not be applicable to other material classes or operating conditions.
The exact improvement in accuracy and the applicability beyond the stated domain remain uncertain.
Experimental phonon thermal conductivity can be compared with model predictions across a range of high-entropy alloys to assess model accuracy.
Time-domain thermoreflectance or laser-induced transient-grating spectroscopy can be used to obtain the relevant phonon thermal-conductivity measurements.
The hypothesis is falsified if the model is not significantly more accurate than current predictions or fails to identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
